clues: This city stands where the plains run up to the Rocky Mountains. Two small creeks flow through it, at the north end of a long mountain front.
Winter cold here keeps breaking in a warm rush of wind. Chinook winds pour down from the peaks and lift some winter days past 50 degrees.
A railroad crew laid out this town in 1867, and the first train rolled in that same year. In 1869, a new governor named it the territory capital.
Each summer, this city throws Frontier Days, a huge rodeo and Old West party. It is the best known show in town, and crowds pack in for it.
The governor of Wyoming works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, in the seat of state rule.
